source.title: ConceptTracer: Interactive Analysis of Concept Saliency and Selectivity in Neural Representations
source.authors: Ricardo Knauer; A. Beinrucker; Erik Rodner

page_placements.theme: Shares of interpretable or polysemantic units outside language models (vision CNNs, ViT/CLIP, audio, tabular, CT encoders)

record.tranche_reason: The study is a full paper about neuron-concept interpretability, but its results concern saliency and selectivity for predefined concepts in a tabular model. It does not test the stated audit shares, language-model generalization, or any of the other claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results about TabPFN neuron-concept associations, a related but different construct from the claim's counts of neuron poles with one or more main jobs. It does not audit Qwen3-32B or other language models, or test explanations on held-out activations. SHAP and optimal-probing comparisons are not rows because they compare methods rather than measure the claim's object; their plotted values are not numerically reported in the text.
record.test_reason: The study builds a tool that scores TabPFN neurons against predefined ICD concepts. TabPFN is a tabular foundation model, not a language model or a vision model. The study does not audit neuron poles or neuron jobs, does not re-read canonical polysemantic neurons, and does not vary architecture or tools to track interpretable share. It builds no neuron-based attribution graphs and does not score explanations on held-out activations. Its measure, significant normalized mutual information with a fixed concept set, is a related but different construct. It does not cite the originals.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is correct. The authors conclude that ConceptTracer facilitates discovering interpretable neurons in TabPFN and offers a framework for exploring how it encodes concept-level information. They also note that sparse probes missed the most selective pairs, so exhaustive search is needed.
record.recipe_differences: The study measures normalized mutual-information-based saliency and selectivity for predefined ICD concepts in a tabular model; it does not use the Qwen pole-audit procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: Selectivity depends on the size and choice of the concept set, as stated in the methods.

fits_no_version.finding: In TabPFN, under 1% of neurons were significantly salient and selective for any of the predefined ICD concepts. This used permutation tests with max-statistic and Bonferroni corrections.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In a tabular foundation model, few neurons align significantly with a fixed set of human-defined domain concepts; supervised concept alignment yields far lower shares than inspection-based audits.

fits_no_version.finding: Pareto-front neuron-concept pairs appeared in initial, middle and final TabPFN layers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In TabPFN, concept-aligned neurons are not concentrated in particular layers.

fits_no_version.finding: Individual TabPFN neurons show differentiation among sub-concepts of one composite input feature (neuron 162). Others show integration across related features (neuron 145).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Some tabular-model neurons encode a coherent higher-level concept spanning related inputs, while others separate sub-concepts.

record.problems: The study uses predefined concepts and states that selectivity depends on the size of the concept set. The main reported significance result is not broken down by task in the text. It does not test whether explanations predict activations on held-out examples.
record.rows_left_out: Section 5.1.3 reports TabPFN test AUC values of 0.79 to 0.85, which do not bear on neuron interpretability. Figure 2 compares sparse-probing baselines, but the text gives no numeric values for those plotted comparisons and they do not measure the claim's object.

untested.parts: Qwen3-32B pole-level shares (about 90% one job, 7% two related jobs, 2–4% not understood).
Other language models, dense and MoE, up to trillions of parameters; TabPFN is not a language model.
InceptionV1 cat-and-car and other canonical polysemantic neurons; recursive generalization versus superposition.
Effect of architecture, regularization and tools on interpretable share; vision-model estimates.
Neuron-based attribution graphs explaining behaviour without a replacement model.
Whether explanations from activating examples predict firing on new inputs.
Simulation-based scoring of neuron explanations on new text.

record.verdict_notes: The relation could be called cites_only or discusses. The paper does not cite the originals; it addresses the related grandmother-cell question of whether single neurons respond to single concepts. The under-1% figure may tempt comparison with V1/V2, but it is a different construct with a different model class and a concept-set-dependent metric. The SHAP and optimal-probing comparisons are method comparisons and are rightly left out.

versions.untested_parts: The Qwen3-32B pole-level shares of one job, two related jobs, and not-yet-understood poles.
Other language models, dense and mixture-of-experts models, and scaling up to trillions of parameters.
InceptionV1 cat-and-car neurons, pose, and recursive generalization versus superposition.
Architecture, regularization, tools, and the stated interpretability estimates for InceptionV1-sized vision models.
Attribution graphs built from a large model's own neurons and whether they explain behavior without replacement models or reconstruction error.
Whether explanations based on activating examples predict where neurons fire on new examples.
Automated scoring of neuron explanations by simulating activations on new text.

rows.subject: TabPFN 6.3.2
rows.operation_detail: Measured significant neuron-concept saliency and selectivity with ConceptTracer.

conditions.value: inhospital mortality, ICU transfer within 12h, critical outcome, hospitalization; reported as an aggregate without taskwise percentages
ICD concepts at three hierarchical levels; concepts with prevalence < 100 were filtered out

rows.measure: Share of neurons significantly salient and selective for specific concepts
rows.note: This is not a count of neuron poles with one or more main jobs; the authors use significance thresholds for associations with their selected concept set.
rows.check: Linking and state are correct. The value counts neurons significantly salient and selective for a predefined ICD concept set, which depends on concept-set size by construction. It is not a share of neurons with one main job, and it is in a tabular model. It should not be compared numerically with V1/V2 shares. The denominator is roughly 24 layers × 192 dimensions of target-column embeddings, which the text implies but does not state as a count.

source_check.locator_found: Section 5.2: 'Less than 1% of the neurons were significantly salient and selective for specific concepts'; setup in 5.1.1-5.1.3 (four tasks, ICD concepts at three levels, prevalence < 100 filtered, TabPFN 6.3.2)

rows.subject: TabPFN 6.3.2
rows.operation_detail: Examined which layers supplied neuron-concept pairs on the global Pareto fronts.

conditions.value: four ED triage tasks; no taskwise breakdown stated

rows.measure: Layer locations of neuron-concept pairs on the global Pareto fronts
rows.value: Pairs came from initial, middle, and final layers; the paper says concepts may not be preferentially represented in particular layers.
rows.note: Layer distribution does not measure the share of neurons with one main job.
rows.check: Linking is correct. The row records the layer location of Pareto-front pairs, not interpretable share. It cannot bear on V4's late-layer claim, because no share-by-layer is given.

rows.subject: TabPFN 6.3.2
rows.operation_detail: Compared the association of neuron 162's activations with ICD concepts.
rows.baseline: E87 association; exact baseline values not stated
rows.value: The saliency and selectivity for E86 were reduced by 0.12 and 0.03, respectively, relative to E87.
rows.note: The paper presents this as differentiation among related concepts within a composite input feature.
rows.check: Linking is correct. This is a single illustrative neuron, and the absolute E87 values are not given, only the reductions for E86 (0.12 saliency, 0.03 selectivity).

rows.subject: TabPFN 6.3.2
rows.operation_detail: Examined concept associations with neuron 145's activations, conditional on ICD code I.
rows.value: Cardiac arrhythmias and hypertension ranked among the top-4 features by mutual information with the neuron's activations.
rows.note: The paper describes this as integration across related input features.
rows.check: Linking is correct. This is a single illustrative neuron with a qualitative top-4 mutual-information ranking and no numbers.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

rows.locator_found: Section 5.2: 'Less than 1% of the neurons were significantly salient and selective for specific concepts'; setup in 5.1.1-5.1.3 (four tasks, ICD concepts at three levels, prevalence < 100 filtered, TabPFN 6.3.2)

relation.reason: It discusses whether single neurons are directly interpretable (grandmother-cell framing) but does not test any version.

tranche.reason: A tool paper that scores TabPFN (tabular model) neurons against predefined ICD concepts. No version names tabular models, and the concept-set measure cannot give the share of neurons with a main job. It neither tests nor uses the claim.

source_check.notes: The under-1% figure depends on the chosen concept set (354, 282 and 24 concepts at the low, mid and high levels); selectivity depends on concept-set size by construction. It is not a count of clean neurons. Test AUCs were 0.79 to 0.85.

statements.correction: Less than 1% of TabPFN 6.3.2 neurons were significantly salient and selective for specific ICD concepts (permutation tests; max-statistic correction, p-values combined by Bonferroni). Aggregate over four MIMIC-IV-ED tasks and three concept levels; no per-task percentages.
